description: An HR business partner must decide whether to authorize Morgan as an internal mediator for recurring handoff disputes between two departments and finalize Morgan's monthly caseload, co-mediator assignment, certification confirmation, and review timing.

shared_context.S1: Two departments have recurring interpersonal disputes during client-handoff work, and the current arrangement does not include a designated internal mediator.
shared_context.S2: Elena is responsible for deciding whether an employee may serve as an internal mediator and for recording the operating conditions.
shared_context.S3: Morgan has expressed interest in helping with the handoff disputes, while Nadia is available to support mediation work.
shared_context.S4: As part of the normal review process, Elena asks the team lead, Morgan, Nadia, and Employee Relations to provide relevant input before she records the decision.

PF1.text: Marcus personally observed Morgan successfully mediate exactly five difficult team disputes over the past six months; those observations were discussed informally and have not been entered into Morgan's development record.

PF2.text: Morgan can sustainably handle no more than two mediation cases per month while maintaining her primary role, a boundary she has not yet raised with Elena because the proposed role is still informal.

PF3.text: Nadia and Morgan made an informal agreement that Nadia would co-mediate Morgan's first cases, but it was never added to the staffing plan because no authorization decision had been made.

PF4.text: Theo checked the current Employee Relations policy this week and confirmed that an internal mediator must have certification explicitly confirmed in the authorization record and must receive a formal review within exactly 60 days; this policy check has not yet been added to Elena's packet.

acceptance_conditions: Morgan must be authorized as an internal mediator.
Exactly five successful observations must be documented as the basis for authorization.
Morgan's monthly mediation caseload must be limited to exactly two cases.
Nadia must be designated as Morgan's co-mediator.
Certification must be explicitly confirmed in the authorization record.
A formal review must be scheduled within exactly 60 days.
The settlement must cite the spoken facts that support the authorization decision.

provenance_checks.P1: 'PF1' in credited_facts and 'PF1' in justification_fact_ids and 'PF1' in revealed

decisive_facts.why: Marcus's five firsthand observations change the authorization from unsupported to approved and change the documented evidence count to exactly 5.
Morgan's stated sustainable limit changes the monthly caseload from an unspecified or larger assignment to exactly 2 cases.
Nadia's informal agreement with Morgan changes the staffing assignment to Nadia as the required co-mediator.
Theo's policy confirmation changes the authorization record by requiring certification confirmation and fixes the formal review deadline at exactly 60 days.
